title: Backflow test retest: close the repair and reporting loop
description: A retest is the documented follow-through after a failed result or service event when the governing program requires a passing verification.
prompt: When is a retest required and what closes it out?
answer: A retest is the documented follow-through after a failed result or service event when the governing program requires a passing verification. Keep the failed finding, repair scope, retest, and filing tied to the same assembly.
urgency: Do not assume a repair invoice is a passing retest. Escalate if the failure mode, model, or required filing path is unclear.
diagramAlt: Backflow service and compliance workflow reference
identifiers: The failed report identifies the test date, assembly, and finding to be resolved.
Repair scope must identify the exact model and component path rather than a generic kit.
The retest result and accepted filing create the final compliance record.

choices.label: I have a notice or program requirement
choices.detail: Use the issuing program to verify deadline and filing requirements.

choices.label: The assembly failed or needs service
choices.detail: Document the device and define repair plus retest scope.

choices.label: I manage a commercial asset
choices.detail: Separate access, shutdown, testing, and closeout responsibilities.

steps.title: Establish the exact record
steps.body: Keep the original failed test and identify the exact assembly before authorizing work.

steps.title: Define the specific scope
steps.body: Confirm who repairs, who retests, and whether the same provider can perform both actions under the local program.

steps.title: Prove the closeout
steps.body: Retain the passing retest and proof of submission or acceptance with the original notice.

safeChecks: Ask whether a retest deadline applies after repair.
Keep model photos before parts are ordered.
Confirm the assembly remains accessible for the return visit.
stopConditions: A repair is proposed without a component-level diagnosis.
There is no confirmed retest or filing responsibility.
notThisDevice: A generic service listing does not establish program eligibility.
A device family is not enough to identify compatible parts.
This page does not replace a qualified assessment or authority approval.
evidenceNote: Use the governing utility or authority requirement and exact manufacturer documentation to validate this specific decision path.
